meaning.zh:
“未受任何惩罚” 或 “逃脱惩罚”。

这个短语起源于古英语中的 “scot”，意为税收或款项。在中世纪，"scot" 是另一种税，指的是某种分摊费用。如果某人 “got off scot-free”，意味着他们逃脱了这种税务或责任，最终这一说法演变为逃避任何形式的惩罚或负担。
meaning.en: This idiom originates from the Old English word “scot,” which referred to a tax or payment. In medieval times, "scot" was a term used for a kind of tax that indicated some form of share. If someone “got off scot-free,” it meant they avoided this tax or responsibility. Over time, it evolved to mean avoiding any form of punishment or burden.

lines.en: He broke the vase but *got off scot-free* because no one saw him.
lines.zh: 他打碎了花瓶，但因为没有人看到他，所以他逃脱了惩罚。

lines.en: Despite the evidence, the suspect *got off scot-free* due to a technicality.
lines.zh: 尽管有证据，由于程序问题，嫌疑人还是未受任何惩罚。

lines.en: It's not fair that he *got off scot-free* while we had to bear the consequences.
lines.zh: 他逃脱了惩罚，而我们却不得不承担后果，这不公平。
